scope_note: Result is limited to searched public official/archive surfaces. Absence from these surfaces is not proof that a record never existed, was destroyed, remains classified, or is concealed.

new_findings: NARA now exposes UAP bulk-download surfaces with machine-readable metadata for Project Blue Book holdings.
Relevant public NARA series include Project Blue Book Case Files NAID/series 595466, sanitized case files 597821, Project Bluebook Artifacts 23857158, and OSI UFO investigations 23857159.

The sanitized Blue Book corpus is available as multiple very large image/PDF bulk packages, while the series metadata are separately exposed. This creates a deterministic retrieval surface rather than an open-ended web hunt.

Department of War PURSUE republishes a government-source historical analysis describing RB-47 as a reported visual/radar/pulsed-microwave multi-channel case, but this is not the original raw sensor stream and does not reopen G3.
targets.next_exact_retrieval: Resolve the 17 July 1957 RB-47 case to exact item/file-unit IDs within NARA 595466/597821 and OSI 23857159; retrieve only the corresponding file-unit bytes before touching the multi-hundred-GB corpus.

new_findings: Department of the Navy FY2023 FOIA log contains request DON-NAVY-2023-012523 explicitly seeking USS Princeton radar returns, E-2C AN/APS-145 returns, air-defense-control-net audio, USS Louisville sonar data, and official reports for 10-16 Nov 2004.
The official disposition for that request is Full Denial - No Records Located.

An official Navy-hosted NASA brief states that aircrew/personnel debriefs validated the event but that there was very limited data to support technical analysis and reporting stopped at 3rd Fleet with no process to share it.
An earlier FY2017 Navy FOIA request also explicitly sought radar data/FLIR and related records for 14 Nov 2004, demonstrating repeated attempts to retrieve the measurement layer.
targets.next_exact_retrieval: Shift from generic sensor-data requests to records-management provenance: retention schedules, data-handling SOPs, exercise data-capture procedures, transfer logs, and destruction/disposition records for the named systems/units and dates.

new_findings: DIA Electronic Reading Room primary JCS/DoD message remains the strongest official event-level object and reports the second F-4 lock at 27 NM, closure 150 NMPH, and an approximately maintained 25 NM range.
DIA FOIA logs show historical public requests specifically targeting the October 1976 report, confirming an official retrieval lineage but not adding raw sensor data.

NARA exposes Tehran political/subject-file archival surfaces from 1976-1978, including Political Subject Files, Tehran, Lot 85 F 132 (HS1-79786561), but no item-level bind to the UAP incident was established in this pass.
Department of War PURSUE republishes secondary government historical discussion of the Tehran incident, but this does not substitute for F-4 or ground-radar telemetry.

pattern_registry_updates.reason: R3 converted generic missing-data claims into named archive/disposition outcomes: one exact No Records Located FOIA result, one massive but targetable NARA archival surface, and one primary narrative report without instrument records.
No target gained common-time calibrated multi-sensor fusion.
All three targeted residuals arose in military/high-instrumentation environments, but the public denominator and retention policies remain poorly matched.

scientific_verdict: R3 DID NOT RECOVER THE PHYSICS-ENABLING MEASUREMENT LAYER. IT DID, HOWEVER, TURN THREE VAGUE 'MISSING DATA' PROBLEMS INTO THREE DIFFERENT TESTABLE ARCHIVAL PROBLEMS: RB47=ITEM-LEVEL NARA RESOLUTION; NIMITZ=CUSTODY/RETENTION/DISPOSITION; TEHRAN=INSTRUMENT/MAINTENANCE/GROUND-RADAR ARCHIVE RECOVERY.

actions: Resolve RB47 to exact NARA file-unit/item IDs using bulk metadata before downloading large binaries.
For Nimitz, search retention/disposition records rather than repeating raw-radar FOIA wording already answered No Records Located.

canonical_seal: THE RAW DATA DID NOT APPEAR, BUT THE SEARCH SPACE COLLAPSED FROM 'FIND UFO FILES' TO NAMED ARCHIVE OBJECTS, CUSTODY CHAINS, AND INSTRUMENT RECORDS.
